title: Midnight wasn't the end: What happened in first few hours of Independent India
content: India's liberation from British rule was celebrated at midnight on August 15, 1947, as Jawaharlal Nehru captivated everyone with his famed 'Tryst with Destiny' speech. Following this historic moment, the newly formed government not only celebrated freedom but also faced daunting challenges related to governance and nation-building, with Lord Mountbatten taking charge as the first Governor-General during a time marked by the chaos of Partition.

title: USS Abraham Lincoln to return home amid rising scrutiny over sailor welfare
content: After an extended deployment, the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier is making its way home. While Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao minimized reports of sailor difficulties and supply deficiencies, the Navy contends that allegations regarding a mental health crisis aboard are overstated. This lengthy deployment highlights the pressures faced by the US Navy's carrier fleet, with the USS George Washington set to take over its operations in the Middle East.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott is leading the charge in medical debt relief, having made groundbreaking donations that freed over $40 billion for families burdened by this often overwhelming responsibility. Her innovative approach, which involves acquiring debt at minimal costs for cancellation, has inspired other billionaires to make similar contributions. Yet, the call for broader policy reform lingers, revealing the constraints of this philanthropic model.

title: Zohran Mamdani’s ‘common sense regulation’ may push Amazon to move NYC deliveries
content: In a bold move, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has shown support for a groundbreaking bill that mandates direct employment for delivery drivers, aiming to eliminate subcontracting and bolster the rights of workers. However, Amazon has raised concerns, indicating the bill may drive its operations outside of the city.

title: Gut bacteria in psychopaths may drive sinful behavior, scientists claim
content: Recent research indicates a potential connection between gut microorganisms and psychopathic traits. The study unveiled variations in gut and oral bacteria among individuals with differing psychopathy scores. Notably, metabolic byproducts such as glucose and taurine reflected distinct patterns across participant groups. These findings suggest a fascinating interplay between gut health and psychological characteristics, warranting further investigation to clarify these complex gut-brain interactions.

title: Airtel discontinues several prepaid plans including one of its most popular
content: Airtel has decided to eliminate several of its prepaid recharge options, including the frequently used Rs 299 plan. As a result, Airtel's prices are set to rise by approximately three to four percent. Customers who relied on the Rs 299 plan will need to transition to the Rs 349 pack, marking a notable increase in their expenses.

title: Govinda hits back at Sunita Ahuja over ‘abusive language’ targeting family
content: Govinda has made a public plea for his wife, Sunita Ahuja, to cease her use of foul language, notably phrases referencing mothers and sisters. Concerned about the effects of such behavior on impressionable youth, the actor highlighted the responsibilities of public figures. Sunita's frank comments about their life together have also caught the public's attention, igniting lively discussions among supporters.

title: 7.7 magnitude Indonesia quake: 38 killed, buildings collapse; 5 visuals of devastation
content: A significant earthquake registering 7.7 on the Richter scale rocked eastern Indonesia early Saturday, claiming the lives of at least thirty-eight individuals and leading to the destruction of various structures. Ongoing rescue missions are striving to aid the affected population, while landslides and widespread power failures hinder relief efforts in some areas. Although a tsunami alert was briefly raised, it was later cancelled after confirming that sea conditions were stable.

title: IPL cricketer Abishek Porel denied bail in alleged rape case
content: Abishek Porel, Delhi Capitals and Bengal cricketer, has been denied bail in an alleged rape and blackmail case involving a medical student. Arrested in Hooghly on August 11, he was sent to 14 days of judicial custody. The complainant alleged he promised marriage, later threatened to share private photos and illegally confined her during an April incident.

(Looks like the sahib is wearing the Tricolour in Urdu. Or perhaps, instead of India, he is celebrating Ireland's Independence Day)." title: MP children fall ill in bid to set Tiranga yatra record

Some students skipped breakfast and faced inadequate water arrangements during the event. Officials stated all students received treatment and were discharged later. Show-cause notices were issued to officials regarding the incident.

title: UK searches for homes with air conditioning jump 104% as heatwaves intensify
content: Searches for homes with air conditioning in the UK have more than doubled this summer. Repeated heatwaves prompt buyers to pay greater attention to property cooling capabilities. Many households are making practical changes to keep cool during hotter weather. Britain's housing stock faces concerns about coping with increasingly hotter summers. This shift influences buyer priorities and what they are willing to purchase.

title: 'Much remains to be done’: CJI urges young lawyers to shoulder responsibility of future

The responsibility of the legal profession will soon rest on their shoulders. He highlighted the historical connection between law and India's freedom struggle. Young lawyers are encouraged to protect and carry forward justice institutions.

title: 'Awarapan 2' OTT release: When and where to stream Emraan Hashmi's film

A sequel to Hashmi's 2007 film 'Awarapan', the movie has already surpassed the lifetime collection of its predecessor on opening day itself, raking in over Rs. 21 crore at the box office despite stiff competition from 'Batwara 1947' and 'Vishwanath & Sons'. title: ‘School thik karo’: Dipke’s 1st audit flags gaps in Hingoli school - watch
content: Abhijeet Dipke launched the 'School Thik Karo' campaign in Santuk Pimpri village.  The campaign seeks a social audit of rural government schools nationwide.  It aims to identify and address issues like lack of water and poor sanitation.  Parents and residents will report deficiencies using a standardized assessment form.  The initiative focuses on essential facilities and improving the learning environment for students.

title: Bangladesh 6 wickets away from historic win as Australia stumble to 161/4

Hasan Mahmud has played a pivotal role, claiming several key wickets for the team. Meanwhile, Mehidy Hasan Miraz has made significant contributions with both bat and ball, putting Australia in a tough position to salvage the match.

title: 'Public services neglected': CJP's new campaign to check facilities at public hospitals

This initiative follows their "School Thik Karo" campaign, which audits the amenities in government schools.  The party founder alleged that patients face long delays and poor facilities in public healthcare.  They aim to document infrastructure deficiencies and treatment access issues in hospitals.  Findings will be used to press for improvements in public education and healthcare.

title: Lucknow-Delhi Tejas becomes India's first privately branded train, 'Sprite' Tejas
content: The Lucknow-Delhi Tejas Express will be known as the Sprite Tejas Express from August 20. Coca-Cola's Sprite unit secured branding rights for the train's name and coaches. This move aims to generate non-fare revenue for the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation. Other companies can also apply for branding on remaining coaches on a first-come basis. This initiative follows the railways' exploration of private participation in train operations.

title: Hazlewood makes Australian Test history, joins elite club with 300th wicket

This achievement underscores Australia's strength, with four bowlers each having over 300 Test wickets on the field together. This historic moment unfolded during the first Test match against Bangladesh in Darwin, with Hazlewood achieving his impressive 14th five-wicket haul as well.

title: 30 Tests, 30 venues: Yashavi Jaiswal follows Sachin Tendulkar's footsteps
content: When Yashasvi Jaiswal walked out to bat in Galle for the first Test against Sri Lanka, he was playing the 30th Test of his career. The milestone came with an unusual record - Jaiswal has played each of his first 30 Tests at a different venue. The India opener has never played a Test at the same ground twice. His journey began in Roseau in July 2023 and, after stops across the Caribbean, South Africa, India, England and Australia, he reached his 30th Test in Galle on Saturday.

title: Emraan Hashmi confirms the possibility of ‘Awarapan 3'

title: The ghost bus of West London: Phantom No 7 linked to 1934 fatal crash
content: The legend of the phantom Number 7 bus haunts a road in North Kensington, intertwining with a tragic accident from 1934. title: Why India's GCC boom is facing a talent problem — and what companies want next

Rising costs and employee pressure are also contributing to the talent challenge.  GCCs need to significantly increase investment in AI-ready talent and skills.  Strengthening talent ecosystems will ensure India's continued leadership in the global GCC landscape.

title: Ukraine offers Black Sea shipping truce; Russia yet to respond : Report
content: a surge in strikes on ships and ports disrupts trade and raises concerns about global food supplies . the proposal was conveyed to Moscow through a third party . it comes as Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of escalating attacks on vessels and ports involved in exports .

title: BJP says Sonia Gandhi tried to stop Vande Mataram at I-Day event; Cong hits back
content: BJP alleges 'hatred' over rendition of full version of Vande Mataram . BJP accuses grand old party's former chief of objecting to national song . opposition party rejects allegation .

title: 'Unfortunate, irresponsible': J&K CM's remarks on Article 370 & PoK draw BJP fire
content: opposition leader says the abrogation of Article 370 strengthened the federal structure in Kashmir . the chief minister's speech was a bit regrettable, he says . opposition leader sunil Sharma accuses him of creating an atmosphere of confusion in the valley .

title: Dad rescues 10-year-old girl from Myrtle Beach rip current, then is swept away
content: Derrick Moore, 47, of Loganville, Ga., helped the girl to safety at Myrtle Beach but was then pulled under . a south Carolina beach vacation turned tragic when a father of four died after swimming into a dangerous rip current to save a young girl .

title: Captain Binface's loss to Farage sums up post-Brexit politics
content: Count Binface poses for the media during the Clacton by-election count . the show has been so off the rails that fans of Yes Minister have even been left wondering if it was too sedate to capture the schizophrenic chicanery of the current era .

title: AI skills, free coaching, sports & jobs: PM Modi's I-Day speech for Gen Z
content: prime minister said one crore youth would be trained in artificial intelligence-related skills . the announcement came as he described AI, quantum technology, robotics and robotics . he linked the Viksit Bharat goal to the country's young population .

title: Strong tremor rocks Indonesia hours after 7.7 magnitude quake claims at least 38 lives
content: 7.7-magnitude quake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region . the epicentre is located at 8.557°S latitude and 121.181°E longitude . at least 38 people were killed, buildings collapsed and communications disrupted .
